extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and advanced creative writers studying narratology and narrative technique
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and production guidance for the temporal organization of narrative focused on iterative (habitual/repeated) vs singulative (single/episodic) modes, their interactions, and the tense/aspect strategies that mark them. Emphasizes techniques (internal determination/specification, pseudo-iterative uses, internal/external diachrony) illustrated with Proustian examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal determination and internal specification (iterative diversification)
rubrics_metrics.description: The two techniques (internal determination and specification) can come into play together in the same section; internal determination (e.g., spring/summer) governs following sentences, while internal specification (e.g., 'on some days, though very rarely') introduces exceptional but non-singulative variants that bear on preceding sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use internal determination to produce regularly recurring variants and internal specification to introduce exceptional variants within an iterative series. Example: the 'returns home' paragraph where an absolute iterative principle is opened then diversified by internal determination (spring/summer) and finally qualified by an internal specification ('on some days, though very rarely').

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative unit as a synthetic temporal form
rubrics_metrics.description: An iterative unit (e.g., 'sleepless night') can be narrated solely in its own successiveness without letting the passage of external years intervene; typic nights remain similar from beginning to end, varying without evolving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing iterative units, maintain their synthetic, self-contained duration; do not necessarily age or historicize them unless intending to show irreversible transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the singulative in service of the iterative (illustration or exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Singulative (single) events may be invoked literally as either (a) illustration and confirmation of an iterative series ('thus, one day Albertine...') or (b) as an exception to an established rule ('Once, however ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate singulative episodes so they either exemplify the habit or deliberately deviate from it, thereby reinforcing the iterative code rather than simply interrupting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pseudo-iterative convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The convention of the pseudo-iterative consists in presenting singular events or singulatives as if they were habitual, thereby making the singulative serve the iterative (a rhetorical/structural trick).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that pseudo-iterative passages can mask chronology or create ambiguity; they are a resource for simulating habit while recounting unique events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal diachrony vs external diachrony (interaction of within-unit time and real-world time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish internal diachrony (the internal duration/unfolding of the syntactic unit) from external diachrony (the real series of days/years separating instances). Iterative narratives can either ignore external diachrony or integrate it, producing irreversible transformations (aging, maturation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether iterative units should remain constant or reflect cumulative external time; arrange episodes to treat internal and external diachronies in parallel when desired (e.g., morning/afternoon/years mapping to stages of life).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternation of iterative and singulative as fundamental rhythmic device
rubrics_metrics.description: Proustian narrative substitutes for the classical alternation of summary and scene a different alternation: iterative and singulative. The rhythm of the Recherche is essentially based on this alternation, which forms its synthetic structure by assimilation and abstraction rather than acceleration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In composing narrative rhythm, consider alternating iterative sections (generalized, habitual material) with singulative scenes (specific events) instead of relying on the classical summary/scene polarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional subordinations between iterative and singulative sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative often overlays a system of functional subordinations: an iterative section may have a descriptive/explanatory function subordinated to (and inserted within) a singulative scene; conversely, a singulative scene may be subordinated to an iterative development to illustrate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map hierarchical relationships among sections (iterative subordinated to singulative, singulative subordinated to iterative, nested parentheses) to clarify their narrative functions and to structure explanations or illustrations within scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex nested structures and possible elision of clear alternation
rubrics_metrics.description: More complex structures exist where iterative and singulative relations nest (e.g., a singular anecdote illustrating an iterative development that is itself subordinated to a singulative scene). Sometimes the narrative passes from one aspect to the other without explicit functional marking, producing effects that resist analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nesting intentionally for depth, but be aware that failure to mark relations can produce interpretive ambiguity; this can be a stylistic device or a source of incoherence depending on authorial intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verbal-aspect/tense as primary marker of iterative vs singulative
rubrics_metrics.description: Tense and aspect choices (imperfect vs passé simple/past definite) are central: imperfects often indicate iterative or concomitant states, while passé simple is used for strictly singulative events. Adverbials like 'suddenly' force iterative imperfects to be read as iterative misuse unless corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent tense/aspect alignment with the intended temporal mode. Watch for adverbials that re-interpret aspect (e.g., 'suddenly' compels a singulative reading) and correct incoherent mixtures to avoid 'inextricable confusion' in temporal aspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of deictic temporal markers to create iterative plateaux
rubrics_metrics.description: Words/phrases such as 'thenceforth', 'since', 'now' treat stories as succession of states substituted for one another and mark iterative plateaux rather than causal trains of events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ deictic markers to shape perceptions of continuity or stasis; they help create iterative modalities where states replace event causality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schematization of temporal systems to reveal immanent structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Schematization (diagramming) of iterative systems is used not to account for 'beauty' but to analyze 'immanent' temporal structures that give the text its skeleton and without which the text would not exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structural diagrams to make explicit the hierarchical and variant relations among determinations/specifications in iterative passages; such schematization reveals hidden complexities underlying apparent continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrospective unity (unity constructed after the fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative's unity can be 'ulterior' or retrospective, a unity imposed after the fact on heterogeneous materials—'a unity that has been unaware of itself, therefore vital and not logical'—which tolerates variety and patchwork origins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that unity can be achieved editorially/retrospectively; this allows patchwork assembly of materials from different periods while still producing a coherent narrative if arranged with care, though fragment resistance may remain visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal coherence as an evaluative criterion (avoidance of 'whitewashing' tricks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempts to 'whitewash' chronological or psychological confusion by daubing verbs with imperfects (making singulatives look iterative) can lead to incoherence; careful editorial correction (e.g., changing an imperfect to a passé simple) can resolve such confusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate narrative passages for coherent temporal aspect; where mixed aspects produce confusion, prefer explicit aspectual marking or editorial corrections to align tense with narrative function rather than concealing contradictions.
